newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK support sends won to close at upper limit.
newsitem.headline: BOK support sends won to close at upper limit.

text.p: The won ended Wednesday's trading at its upper limit as corporations rushed to sell dollars after the central Bank of Korea (BOK) took an aggressive stance in support of the local unit, traders said.
The won close at its limit of 859.00, compared with Tuesday's close of 870.50. It opened at a day low of 865.00.
After the won surged to its limit, dollar buying sentiment became so frozen the BOK bid to absorb dollars, traders said.
"Today was a stop-loss market," said a western bank dealer. "The market moved in reaction to the BOK's recent comments."

On Tuesday, a senior BOK official said the bank would seek strong measures to stabilise won's sharp depreciation. The central bank has recently been actively selling dollars to slow the won's fall, dealers said.
The central bank has refused to confirm or deny talk of its intervention in the interbank market.
A foreign bank dealer said that he expected corporate selling would continue on Thursday.
"A key factor is the speculative dollar positions bought by corporates and how much they are going to sell off," he said.
But fundamental factors continue to point to a strong dollar, traders said. The local unit is under pressure from the dollar's continued strength on world markets, a snowballing trade deficit.
"In the short term, the dollar will go down because of the central bank, but it will be hard to keep the dollar down unless the greenback weakens overseas," a local trader said.
Dealers said the won could rise to around the 853 level on Thursday.
Thursday's base mid-rate was pegged at 859.30, against Wednesday's 878.70. -- Katherine Bruce (822) 727 5644
